domain: Biblical Hermeneutics / Religious Ethics / Commitment System Analysis
topic_summary: Analysis of Deuteronomy 7's herem command—the directive to destroy or expel certain peoples and prohibit covenantal mixing. The passage functions as a contested kernel where different interpretive communities read the same text to instantiate fundamentally different constraint structures governing identity boundaries, violence legitimacy, and intergroup relations.

key_entities: Deuteronomy 7:1-5 (textual kernel: command to destroy/expel seven nations, prohibition on intermarriage)
Interpretive authority structures (rabbinic tradition, Christian supersessionism, secular biblical criticism)
Contemporary ethnoreligious communities (Jewish, Christian, Islamic groups with distinct reading traditions)
Historical conquest narratives (Joshua, Judges as implementation texts)
Modern human rights frameworks (universal dignity claims that contest particularist readings)
Purity-boundary enforcement mechanisms (marriage law, apostasy rules, convert status)
key_tensions: Durable divine command vs. historically-bounded situational directive
Particularist covenantal identity vs. universalist ethical inclusion
key_claims: Reading A: Text encodes timeless separation mandate grounding identity through exclusion
Reading B: Text reflects ancient Near Eastern context, morally superseded or allegorized
Intermediate positions exist (Maimonidean 'seven nations extinct' doctrine, Christian typological reframing)
Constraint structure changes fundamentally between readings (who enters victim set, what legitimates violence)
mechanisms: Halakhic marriage prohibition enforcement (Jewish communities implementing Deuteronomy 7:3)
Colonial-era appropriation of conquest narrative (settler ideologies citing herem as template)
Allegorical displacement (Christian exegesis reframing 'nations' as vices or spiritual enemies)
absences: No engagement with victim communities' counter-readings (Canaanite descendants, colonized peoples)
Limited analysis of enforcement divergence (why some communities operationalize herem, others don't)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Deuteronomy 7:1-5's command structure: destroy/expel designated peoples, prohibit intermarriage, maintain covenantal separation
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Scriptural fixity plus interpretive tradition—rabbinic, patristic, reformed, critical-historical—each claiming authoritative reading of unchangeable text
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Interpretive Elasticity (Pattern 3)—kernel remains textually fixed while interpretive layer absorbs radical shifts in applied constraint without surfacing revision

readings.commitment: Herem encodes timeless divine mandate for identity preservation through bounded membership and categorical separation from designated outsiders
readings.authority_grounding: Scriptural literalism plus covenantal continuity (text as perpetual law requiring obedience)
readings.expected_structural_delta: High extractiveness on intermarriage autonomy, expansive victim set (all non-covenant outsiders as potential contamination threat), violence legitimation through divine command obedience

readings.commitment: Herem was historically-bounded directive for ancient Israel's settlement period, morally superseded by prophetic universalism or Christian covenant
readings.authority_grounding: Historical-critical method or progressive revelation theology (later texts/covenants override earlier particularism)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low extractiveness on intermarriage (constraint removed or relocated to consent/belief rather than ethnicity), narrow victim set (only those coerced by residual fundamentalist enforcement), violence delegitimated through ethical supersession

readings.commitment: Herem's 'nations' are typological placeholders for spiritual enemies (sin, temptation) not ethnic groups; conquest is internal moral warfare
readings.authority_grounding: Patristic-medieval Christian exegesis or kabbalistic-mystical Jewish interpretation (text's plain sense transcended by hidden meaning)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Zero extractiveness on interethnic relations (constraint relocated entirely to internal spiritual domain), victim set collapses to abstract vices, violence reframed as metaphorical self-discipline

axiom_contradictions.basis: Durable reading's axiom (divine command permanence requires ongoing obedience to separation mandate) cannot coexist with supersession reading's axiom (later moral revelation overrides earlier particularist commands) in any single coherent framework—accepting supersession as true requires rejecting command permanence as false

Durable reading's axiom (text's plain-sense command targets ethnic outsiders) is incompatible with allegorical reading's axiom (text's true referent is non-ethnic spiritual domain)—no framework can hold both the plain sense as binding AND the plain sense as transcended simultaneously

axes.structural_delta: Timeless divine command requiring categorical separation and exclusion of designated outsiders to preserve covenantal identity
axes.primary_observable: Marriage law enforcement patterns in communities reading Deuteronomy 7 as perpetually binding; frequency of herem-derived identity boundary policing
axes.selection_reason: Highest extractiveness reading; distinct beneficiary/victim structure; captures maximum constraint load of literalist interpretation

axes.structural_delta: Herem as historically-bounded ancient directive, morally superseded by later prophetic universalism or Christian covenant, removing ethnic exclusion constraint
axes.primary_observable: Denominational policy on interfaith marriage; scholarly consensus on Deuteronomy 7's applicability; human rights framework adoption in religious communities
axes.selection_reason: Structurally inverse to Reading 1; captures constraint-removal dynamics; distinct authority grounding (critical scholarship vs scriptural literalism)

axes.structural_delta: Herem's 'nations' reframed as spiritual enemies not ethnic groups; constraint relocated from interethnic relations to internal moral discipline
axes.primary_observable: Exegetical tradition citation patterns; absence of herem language in interfaith policy despite scriptural centrality; prevalence of 'spiritual warfare' metaphor adoption
axes.selection_reason: Third structural position—neither enforces nor supersedes but displaces constraint domain entirely; captures interpretive elasticity mechanism

axes.human_readable: Maimonidean Extinction Doctrine (Seven Nations No Longer Exist)
axes.structural_delta: Herem remains theoretically binding but pragmatically nullified because target populations extinct; constraint exists in principle but cannot be actualized
axes.primary_observable: Halakhic responsa on Deuteronomy 7 applicability; rabbinic rulings on convert acceptance from historically 'prohibited' groups
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: intermediate position between durable and supersession readings; piton structure (atrophied enforcement) captured implicitly in Reading 1's generative range

axes.structural_delta: Settler colonial movements appropriating Deuteronomy 7 conquest template to legitimate indigenous dispossession
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of Deuteronomy 7 citation in colonial-era religious justifications for land seizure; contemporary nationalist movements invoking herem framework
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: downstream application of Reading 1 rather than independent reading of kernel itself; high epsilon but structurally derivative

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Herem binding in principle but target populations extinct, nullifying practical enforcement
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Intermediate position between selected readings; piton structure (atrophied constraint) implicitly captured in Reading 1's generative range as edge case

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Settler colonial appropriation of Deuteronomy 7 conquest template to legitimate dispossession
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Downstream application of durable_separation_reading rather than independent kernel reading; derivative structural position despite high extractiveness

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected.
